mainTopic: Does רבי יהודה's rule that a second twin 'is like it does not exist' (וָלָד שֵׁנִי כְּמַאן דְּלֵיתֵיהּ דָּמֵי) apply only to the קרבן, or also to טומאה and טהרה?
overview: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה's rule, that a second twin is treated as if it does not exist, applies only to the יולדת's קרבן or also to טומאה and טהרה. Another possibility is that he counts the second twin only when it makes things stricter. רב הונא מסורא tries to prove the answer from a ברייתא that lets the קרבן פסח be brought for a יולדת on day 40 or 80, which רב חסדא explained as following רבי יהודה. The גמרא rejects the proof. It reads the ברייתא as a פסח הבא בטומאה and works through what that means for immersion, a טבול יום and a מחוסר כפורים. It also gives רבא's reading, from רב אשי: an early, bloodless miscarriage before the fetus is formed. רבי שמעיה then brings a ברייתא saying the sixty days of purity after a girl must be continuous, and argues it must follow רבי יהודה. The גמרא shows it can fit רבנן too, in a case of twins, a girl and then a boy. Finally אביי brings a similar ברייתא about the thirty days after a boy, and the גמרא begins to ask whose view it is; that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה's rule apply to impurity too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה holds about טומאה. One possibility is that his rule, that the second twin is like it doesn't exist, applies only to the קרבן. For טומאה, the second birth would count and would interrupt the first birth's ימי טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רבי יהודה say about impurity? Maybe he said the second baby 'doesn't exist' only for the offering, because the time to bring the offering had not yet passed. But for impurity and purity, maybe he holds the second baby does count. Then the second birth's impurity interrupts. She finishes the first birth's purity days afterward, and then counts the second birth's days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a question: does רבי יהודה's rule about the second twin apply only to the קרבן, or also to טומאה and טהרה? This step lays out the first side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the קרבן, רבי יהודה ignores the second twin because the time for the first birth's קרבן has not yet passed, so one קרבן covers both. For טומאה, perhaps the second birth does count. Then its days of טומאה cut into the first birth's ימי טהרה, and the leftover days of טהרה are finished afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: The second offspring, meaning a twin born after the first
It is considered as if it does not exist
It is considered as if it does exist
It interrupts, meaning it cuts into the earlier count
Days of purity after birth, when blood she sees does not make her טמאה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two areas. רבי יהודה's known ruling is about the קרבן. The question here is only whether the same rule carries over to טומאה and טהרה.

phrases.aramaic: בְּטוּמְאָה מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה?

phrases.english: that is fit for bringing an offering, and since that is so,
the second offspring is like something that does not exist,
but regarding impurity and purity,

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּטוּמְאָה מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה? מִי אָמְרִינַן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's rule that the second twin is like it doesn't exist extends from the קרבן to טומאה and טהרה.

steps.title: Maybe he only applies it to be strict
steps.stepSummary: This is the other side of the question. Perhaps רבי יהודה treats the second twin as existing only when that leads to a חומרא. Here it would lead to a קולא, because she gets ימי טהרה back, so he would not hold it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe רבי יהודה only uses this idea when it makes things stricter. Here it would make things more lenient, and he does not hold it for a leniency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of its question. Maybe רבי יהודה would not count the second twin for טומאה, since doing so here would be a קולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting the second birth would let her finish the first birth's ימי טהרה later, and during those days blood does not make her טמאה. That is a leniency. If רבי יהודה only counts the second twin to be strict, he would not do it here.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps; it introduces the other side of a question
A stringency
A leniency

phrases.english: Or perhaps, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
it is a stringency that he holds,
but here it is a leniency,
and a leniency he does not hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה חוּמְרָא הוּא דְּאִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the second side of the question opened in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה applies 'the second twin exists' only for stringencies.

steps.title: A teaching about a new mother and the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא מסורא begins a proof from a ברייתא. For a יולדת, the קרבן פסח may be slaughtered and its blood sprinkled for her on the 40th day after a boy or the 80th day after a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא מסורא said: Come and hear. For a woman who gave birth, we slaughter and sprinkle the קרבן פסח on her behalf on the 40th day for a boy and the 80th day for a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. This step only quotes the source; the גמרא will first examine it before the proof is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets the קרבן פסח be brought for her on the 40th or 80th day. That implies she will be fit to eat it that night. The גמרא is about to question how that can be.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has given birth
We slaughter and sprinkle the blood on her behalf
The פסח offering, brought on the 14th of ניסן and eaten that night

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מִסּוּרָא, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rav Huna from Sura said: Come and hear:
A woman after childbirth: we slaughter and sprinkle on her behalf
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is talking about the קרבן פסח on the 14th of ניסן.

phrases.english: on the fortieth day for a male
and on the eightieth day for a female.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מִסּוּרָא, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to resolve the question of steps 1 and 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה counts the second twin for טומאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about bringing the קרבן פסח for a יולדת on day 40 or 80.

steps.title: But she is still impure that night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. On the 40th or 80th day she is still טמאה, because she brings her own קרבן only the next day. So how could she eat the קרבן פסח that night?
steps.simpleTranslation: Really? She is still impure!
steps.whatsHappening: Before using the ברייתא as a proof, the גמרא asks how it can be true: on that day the woman is still טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יולדת may eat קדשים only after bringing her קרבן on day 41 for a boy or day 81 for a girl. On day 40 or 80 she still cannot eat that night. So the ברייתא seems to contradict the basic counting of her days.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'until here?'; here it means 'Is that so?'
Ritually impure

phrases.english: Is that so? She is impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the ברייתא that the קרבן פסח is brought for her on day 40 or 80.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On those days she is still טמאה and cannot eat קדשים until after her own קרבן the next day.

steps.title: The teaching follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who holds the second twin is like it doesn't exist. The case is twins born on two days, so day 40 of the second birth is already day 41 of the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה, who says the second offspring is like it does not exist.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. This also sets up the proof the גמרא will draw for its question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is twins born on two days in a row. On the 14th it is day 40 from the second birth but day 41 from the first, which is the day the first birth's קרבן is due. Since רבי יהודה ignores the second twin, she brings that קרבן and can eat the פסח that night.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this? Used to tie a teaching to a specific sage
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה
The 41st day, when a mother of a boy brings her קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the קרבן פסח follows רבי יהודה: the second twin is ignored, so the first birth's count decides. This is the base for רב הונא's proof.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
the second offspring is like something that does not exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by assigning the ברייתא to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution of the ברייתא to a specific תנא, together with a specific case (twins on two days).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to let a woman who is still טמאה eat the קרבן פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי יהודה, the second twin is ignored, so she counts from the first birth and is already able to bring her קרבן.

steps.title: Finishing the proof: the second twin doesn't count for טומאה either
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה counted the second twin for טומאה, she could not eat the פסח on the night after day 40. So he must hold that the second twin doesn't count for טומאה and טהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say רבי יהודה holds that for טומאה the second child counts as existing, how can we slaughter the פסח for her on day forty? Even that night she still could not eat it! So we must learn that for both טהרה and טומאה, רבי יהודה holds the second child is like it doesn't exist.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רב הונא מסורא's proof using רב חסדא's explanation of the ברייתא. It concludes that רבי יהודה ignores the second twin even for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the ברייתא's day 40 is counted from the second twin. If the second twin restarted her טומאה, on day 40 of the second birth she would still be טמאה, and she would still not be able to eat that night. The ברייתא only works if the second twin is ignored, so day 40 of the second birth is really day 41 of the first.

keyTerms.meaning: The second child (the second twin)
It is treated as if it exists
It is treated as if it does not exist
In the evening, at night (when the פסח is eaten)
Learn from this (a proof is concluded)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not a new proof. It is the end of the proof רב הונא מסורא started in step 3, built on רב חסדא's answer in step 5.

phrases.english: And if you say that regarding impurity
Rabbi Yehuda holds
the second child is like something that exists
how can we slaughter for her on day forty?
phrases.notes: Day forty here is counted from the second twin, the way רב חסדא explained it.

phrases.english: Even at night she cannot eat it!
Rather, must we not learn from this

phrases.aramaic: לְטׇהֳרָה וּלְטוּמְאָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: that for purity and for impurity Rabbi Yehuda holds
the second child is like something that does not exist!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב חסדא's explanation from step 5 to answer the question from steps 1-2.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה ignores the second twin for טומאה and טהרה too.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא allowing the פסח to be slaughtered for a יולדת on day 40, as explained by רב חסדא.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: the ברייתא is about a פסח brought in impurity
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. רבי יהודה may still count the second twin for טומאה, and the ברייתא may be about a פסח הבא בטומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, I can tell you that for טומאה and טהרה, רבי יהודה holds the second child counts as existing. When that ברייתא was taught, it was about a פסח brought in impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It offers another way to read the ברייתא that does not involve twins at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If most of the people are טמא, the פסח is brought בטומאה, and people who are טמא may eat it. So the ברייתא could be about one child and a פסח הבא בטומאה, where her being טמאה would not stop her. Then it proves nothing about how רבי יהודה treats the second twin.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, I can tell you (a way to reject a proof)
A קרבן פסח brought when most of the people are טמא

phrases.english: Actually, I can tell you

phrases.aramaic: לְטוּמְאָה וּלְטׇהֳרָה סְבִירָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: for impurity and purity Rabbi Yehuda holds
that the second child is like something that exists
and when that ברייתא was taught
it was about a Pesach offering brought in impurity

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 6 by placing the ברייתא in a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא does not have to be about twins. It can be about a single birth with a פסח הבא בטומאה.

steps.title: A יולדת doesn't eat even a פסח brought in impurity
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in פסחים says יולדות may not eat a פסח הבא בטומאה. So how could the ברייתא let her eat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But does she eat it? We learned in a משנה: a פסח brought in impurity may not be eaten by זבים, זבות, נדות, and יולדות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection from step 7. It quotes a משנה that says a יולדת may not eat even a פסח הבא בטומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח הבא בטומאה permits people who are טמא from a dead body. It does not permit those whose טומאה comes from their own body, like a יולדת. So step 7's reading seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: But does she eat? (a challenge)
Men and women made טמא by an unusual discharge
Women who are טמאות from their monthly period
Women who are טמאות after giving birth

phrases.english: But does she eat it?
But didn't we learn in a משנה
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in פסחים 95b.

phrases.english: a Pesach offering brought in impurity
zavim and zavot may not eat from it
nor menstruating women and women after childbirth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new reading of the ברייתא offered in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that the ברייתא is about a פסח הבא בטומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says יולדות may not eat a פסח הבא בטומאה, so the ברייתא cannot mean that case.

steps.title: The משנה means women who have not yet immersed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about women who have not immersed. In the ברייתא she has already immersed, so she may eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that משנה, they don't eat because they have not immersed. When the ברייתא teaches that we slaughter and sprinkle for her, it is because she has already immersed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the reading from step 7. It shows that the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is whether she went to the מקוה. A יולדת who has not immersed cannot eat even a פסח הבא בטומאה. One who has immersed, after her first days of טומאה, may eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersion in a מקוה
Slaughtering the animal and sprinkling its blood

phrases.english: In that case, they don't eat
because they did not immerse
When that ברייתא was taught
phrases.notes: Here 'that' means the ברייתא about the יולדת, not the משנה.

phrases.english: that we slaughter and sprinkle for her
it is because she has immersed

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא, לָא אָכְלָן כִּי לָא טְבִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by telling apart the case of the משנה from the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Telling apart two cases (immersed versus not immersed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה bans every יולדת from eating a פסח הבא בטומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה bans only a יולדת who has not immersed. The ברייתא is about one who has.

steps.title: Then she should be fit from day eight
steps.stepSummary: If immersion is enough, she is fit from day eight after a boy. So why does the ברייתא say day forty?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, she should be fit from the boy's eighth day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 9. If immersion is what counts, the ברייתא's day 40 makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a boy, a יולדת immerses at the end of seven days, so she has already immersed by day eight. Under step 9's answer, the ברייתא should have said day 8, not day 40. The fact that it says day 40 shows the reading from step 7 is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (pointing out a problem in the last answer)
The eighth day after the birth
She is fit (allowed)

phrases.english: If so
it is from his eighth day that she is fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מִשְּׁמִינִי דִּילַיהּ הוּא דְּחַזְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 9 by showing it clashes with the ברייתא's day 40.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 9 that the ברייתא is about a יולדת who immersed and a פסח הבא בטומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If immersion is enough, she is fit from day 8, so the ברייתא would have no reason to say day 40.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge weakens the rejection from step 7. That puts the proof about רבי יהודה's view back in play.

steps.title: Not fit from day eight, because a טבול יום of a זב is like a זב
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of the ברייתא holds that a טבול יום of a זב is like a זב, so she cannot eat the פסח from day eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the eighth day she is not fit. He holds that a זב who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall is treated like a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 10. Immersing alone is not enough to let her eat on day eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, we assumed that once she immersed she could eat a פסח הבא בטומאה. Now the גמרא says the תנא treats someone who immersed but whose day is not finished (a טבול יום) as still a זב. A woman after birth is in a similar in-between state until day forty, so she cannot eat before then.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall to finish becoming טהור
A man made טמא by an unusual discharge, a severe kind of טומאה
He is treated like a זב
She is fit (allowed)

phrases.english: From the eighth day she is not fit,
because he holds:
a זב who immersed today is like a זב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the תנא's view on the status of a טבול יום
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once she immerses after seven days, she should be fit to eat from day eight.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא holds that a טבול יום of a זב is like a זב, so she is not fit until day forty.

steps.title: Then she should not be fit on day forty either
steps.stepSummary: If she is still like a זב, then on day forty she still has not brought her קרבן, so she should still not be fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, she should also not be fit on day forty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after day forty she has not yet brought her atonement קרבן. If being 'not fully finished' makes her like a זב, she should still be unfit on day forty. So why does the ברייתא let her eat then?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Also

phrases.english: If so,
on day forty she should also not be fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בְּיוֹם אַרְבָּעִים נָמֵי לָא חַזְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that she is unfit until day forty because she is still like a זב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On day forty she still lacks her קרבן, so by the same reasoning she should still be like a זב.

steps.title: On day forty she is fit, because a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is not like a זב
steps.stepSummary: The תנא separates the two stages. A טבול יום is like a זב, but a מחוסר כפורים is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. On day forty she is fit, because he holds that a זב who is only missing his atonement קרבן is not treated like a זב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the two stages of becoming טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two stages: (1) after immersing, before the day ends (טבול יום), and (2) after the day ends, before bringing the קרבן (מחוסר כפורים). This תנא holds that stage 1 still counts as a זב, but stage 2 does not. So she cannot eat from day eight, but she can eat after day forty even before bringing her קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: No, that is not so
Someone who is fully טהור except that he has not yet brought his atonement קרבן
He is not treated like a זב

phrases.english: No,
on day forty she is fit,
because he holds:

phrases.aramaic: מְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים דְּזָב – לָאו כְּזָב דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: a זב who is missing only his atonement is not like a זב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes between two stages of purification
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a טבול יום is like a זב, a מחוסר כפורים should be too.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תנא holds a טבול יום is like a זב, but a מחוסר כפורים is not.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this תנא: a טבול יום of a זב is like a זב, but a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is not. That is why she eats from day forty and not from day eight.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two stages. A טבול יום has immersed but the day has not ended. A מחוסר כפורים is past nightfall and is missing only the קרבן.

steps.title: How does רבא explain the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is like a זב, so the answer in Step 13 does not work for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, who says a זב who is missing his atonement is like a זב, how does he explain this ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבא, who disagrees with the answer just given, would explain the ברייתא. This sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13's answer depended on a מחוסר כפורים not being like a זב. רבא holds the opposite. For him, on day forty she is still missing her קרבן and should be unfit, so he needs a different explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים (here, the ברייתא)
Explains it (resolves the difficulty)

phrases.english: And according to רבא,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים דְּזָב כְּזָב דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: who says a זב missing his atonement is like a זב,
how does he explain this ברייתא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of Step 13 does not fit רבא's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the ברייתא works according to רבא, who holds a מחוסר כפורים of a זב is like a זב.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא is about a miscarriage before the fetus is formed
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads 'day forty' as day forty after conception of a male, or day eighty for a female, following רבי ישמעאל. Before that the fetus is not formed, so there is no birth טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רבא explains it as day forty from the forming of a male and day eighty from the forming of a female. It follows רבי ישמעאל, who says a male takes forty-one days and a female takes eighty-one days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives רבא's explanation. The ברייתא is about a miscarriage that came too early to count as a birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל, a male fetus is formed only on day forty-one and a female only on day eighty-one. A miscarriage on day forty (male) or day eighty (female) is therefore not a 'birth'. So she has no birth טומאה and never needs a קרבן, and רבא's view about a מחוסר כפורים never comes up.

keyTerms.meaning: The forming of a male fetus (counted from conception)
The forming of a female fetus

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
רבא explains it as:
on day forty from the forming of a male
phrases.notes: Counted from conception, not from birth. She miscarried on that day.

phrases.english: and on day eighty from the forming of a female,
and it follows רבי ישמעאל,
who says: for a male, forty-one days,
for a female, eighty-one days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: רָבָא מְתָרֵץ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14 by redefining the case in the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is about a miscarriage on day forty (male) or day eighty (female) from conception, which according to רבי ישמעאל is before the fetus is formed. So there is no birth טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation changes the case completely. It is no longer about a woman after a real birth, so it says nothing about the need for a קרבן.

steps.title: She should still be טמאה as a נדה
steps.stepSummary: Even if there is no birth טומאה, the miscarriage should make her a נדה, so she should still be unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, she should be טמאה anyway because of being a נדה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking away the birth טומאה does not help if the miscarriage comes with blood, because blood makes her a נדה. A נדה cannot eat the פסח. So the problem returns.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, either way
I should conclude (that) anyway
A woman who is טמאה because of menstrual-type bleeding

phrases.english: In the end,
I should conclude that she is טמאה
because she is a נדה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that she is fit because there was no birth טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A miscarriage usually comes with blood, which makes her a נדה, so she should still be unfit.

steps.title: It was a dry birth
steps.stepSummary: The case is a miscarriage with no blood at all, so there is no נדה טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case of a dry birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a miscarriage that came out with no blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no blood there is no נדה טומאה. With no formed fetus there is no birth טומאה. So she is fully טהורה and may eat.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'dry birth', with no blood coming out

phrases.english: In a case of a dry birth.
phrases.notes: A miscarriage that came out with no blood at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A miscarriage brings blood, so she is a נדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a dry birth with no blood, so there is no נדה טומאה.

steps.title: Then why teach it at all?
steps.stepSummary: If there is no blood and no formed fetus, it is obvious that she is טהורה, so why does the ברייתא need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what new thing the ברייתא teaches, since the ruling now seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there is no birth and no blood, there is no reason to think she is טמאה. A teaching that states something obvious needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Why say it? (It seems obvious)

phrases.english: If so,
why say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא, given the case set up in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא as explained in Steps 15 and 17
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there is no blood and no formed fetus, her being טהורה is obvious, so the ברייתא seems pointless.

steps.title: We might have thought the womb cannot open without blood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that a womb can open without blood, so a dry birth does not make her טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that the womb cannot open without blood. So it teaches us that the womb can open without blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא is teaching, which closes the explanation of the ברייתא according to רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this teaching we might assume that whenever the womb opens, some blood must come out, even if no one saw it, and so she would be a נדה. The ברייתא teaches that this is not so. That means this ברייתא cannot prove anything about רבי יהודה's view on the second twin.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said...
It teaches us
The opening of the womb

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא (as רב אשי explains), the ברייתא is about an early, bloodless miscarriage. It teaches that the womb can open without blood, so it gives no proof about רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִפְתִיחַת הַקֶּבֶר בְּלֹא דָּם,
phrases.english: it is impossible for the womb to open without blood,
phrases.notes: 'קבר' here literally means 'grave', but it is a word for the womb.

phrases.english: so it teaches us
that it is possible for the womb to open without blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a mistaken assumption the ברייתא comes to correct
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A womb can never open without blood, so she would be a נדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A womb can open without blood. A dry miscarriage before the fetus is formed leaves her טהורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes רבא's reading of the ברייתא. It gives a second way, different from the פסח הבא בטומאה reading in Step 7, to show that the ברייתא proves nothing about רבי יהודה's view on the second twin.

steps.title: The sixty days of purity must be continuous
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעיה quotes a ברייתא: the word 'day' teaches that the sixty days of purity after a girl must come one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעיה said: Come and hear. The verse says 'sixty.' You might think the days can be either in a row or spread out. So the verse adds 'day': just as one day is one unbroken stretch, all sixty days must be in a row.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעיה brings a ברייתא to help answer the question about רבי יהודה. This step quotes the source, and the next steps work out what it proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a woman gives birth to a girl, the תורה gives her sixty-six days of purity. The ברייתא reads the word 'day' as teaching that these days cannot be broken up into pieces. The proof depends on who could even imagine the days being broken up.

keyTerms.meaning: continuous, one right after another
scattered, spread out with breaks in between
'one might think', introducing a possibility that the verse will rule out
'the verse teaches', bringing a word from the פסוק to settle the question

phrases.english: Rabbi Shemaya said: Come and hear:
"Sixty": one might think, whether continuous or scattered?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:5, the days of purity after giving birth to a girl.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "day,"

phrases.aramaic: מָה יוֹם רָצוּף – אַף שִׁשִּׁים כּוּלָּן רְצוּפִין.
phrases.english: just as a day is continuous, so too all sixty are continuous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new proof about how רבי יהודה treats the second birth.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה counts the second birth only to be strict
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on 'sixty days' in ויקרא 12:5

steps.title: Whose opinion is this ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who wrote the ברייתא and says it cannot be רבנן, because they never have days that get spread out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבנן, do רבנן even have a case of scattered days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which opinion the ברייתא follows. It sets things up to say the ברייתא must be רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only makes sense if someone might think the days could be split. רבנן start counting fresh from the second baby, so for them the days are never split. So the ברייתא seems not to fit רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'whose is it?', asking which opinion a teaching follows
'if you say', trying out a possible answer

phrases.english: Whose is it? If you say the Rabbis,
do the Rabbis have scattered days at all?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose opinion the ברייתא quoted in step 20 follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It cannot be רבנן, since for them the days are never scattered.

steps.title: So רבי יהודה uses the second birth only to be strict
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be רבי יהודה. Since he demands sixty days in a row, he does not let the second birth bring a leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be רבי יהודה. Since he gives her sixty days that must all be in a row, learn from this: רבי יהודה uses the second birth to be strict, but not to be lenient!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי שמעיה's proof. The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and that answers the question about him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency would be letting her stop for the second birth and then go back to the first birth's purity days, which would split them up. The ברייתא says the sixty days must be in a row, so this leniency is not allowed. So for רבי יהודה the second birth counts only when it makes things stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'rather, is it not...?', pushing toward the only answer left
a strictness
a leniency
'learn from it', drawing a conclusion

phrases.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda?

phrases.aramaic: וּמִדְּקָא יָהֵיב לַהּ שִׁשִּׁים רְצוּפִים בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: And since he gives her sixty continuous days together,
learn from it: he holds of the strictness,
but Rabbi Yehuda does not hold of the leniency!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer in step 21 to finish the proof.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה counts the second birth for strictness only
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא requiring sixty continuous days, read as רבי יהודה

steps.title: No, the ברייתא can follow רבנן: a boy born inside the girl's eighty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof and says the ברייתא follows רבנן, in a case where a boy is born during the eighty days after a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really it is רבנן. What case are we talking about? A woman who gives birth to a boy within the eighty days after a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי שמעיה's proof. It offers a case where the ברייתא could fit רבנן after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא can follow רבנן, it tells us nothing about רבי יהודה, and the proof falls apart. The suggested case is a boy born while she is still within the girl's eighty days. The idea is that the boy's shorter period sits inside the girl's period, so she just finishes the girl's days.

keyTerms.meaning: 'really', keeping the original reading against the challenge
'what case are we dealing with here?', narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case
a woman who has given birth

phrases.english: No, really it is the Rabbis.
And what are we dealing with here?

phrases.aramaic: לְיוֹלֶדֶת זָכָר מִתּוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים שֶׁל נְקֵבָה.
phrases.english: With a woman who gives birth to a male within the eighty days of a female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 22 by fitting the ברייתא to רבנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ברייתא must follow רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There may be a case where רבנן also deal with split days.

steps.title: That case does not work for רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רבנן count from the second baby, so the girl's days end while the boy's days are not done. The first count is simply dropped.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, the first baby's days get finished while the second baby's days are not yet finished, because רבנן count from the second baby!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the case it just suggested. It shows that the case does not really fit רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן the count follows the second baby, so the first baby's count is not what matters. So in this case there is no point in teaching that the girl's sixty days must be in a row. The case suggested in step 23 is pushed aside.

keyTerms.meaning: 'in the end', 'when all is said and done'
the first one (here, the first baby)
the later one (here, the second baby)

phrases.english: In the end, the days of the first are completed,
while up to this point those of the latter are not completed,
for the Rabbis count for the second child!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case proposed in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a boy born within the girl's eighty days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבנן count from the second baby, so the first baby's sixty days are not what she follows.

steps.title: A twins case where רבנן do have split days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new case for רבנן: twins, a girl first and a boy later, with the boy born on day twenty of her purity days, so she must keep seven טמאה days for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you find it for רבנן with a woman who has twins, a girl first and a boy afterward. For example, she gave birth to the later boy on the twentieth of her days of purity, so she must keep seven days of birth טומאה for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a new case where רבנן would also face split days. This step sets up the case, and the next step shows how the ברייתא reads in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boy comes in the middle of the girl's purity days, so she must stop and keep seven days of טומאה for him. That stop breaks up her purity days, so the question of split days becomes real even for רבנן. If this works, the ברייתא can follow רבנן and the proof about רבי יהודה falls.

keyTerms.meaning: 'you can find it', showing a case where something happens
twins
days of purity after birth
the טומאה that comes from giving birth

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two counts: the girl's days of purity were already running, and the boy's seven טמאה days interrupt them in the middle.

phrases.english: Rather, you find it according to the Rabbis
with a woman who gives birth to twins,
the female first and the male later,
and for example, she gave birth to the later male
on the twentieth of the days of purity,

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָעֲיָא מִינְקָט לֵיהּ שִׁבְעָה יוֹמֵי טוּמְאָה דְּלֵידָה
phrases.english: so that she must keep for him seven days of birth impurity
(twins, female),
phrases.notes: Some versions have these words in round brackets, but the corrected wording leaves them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case from step 23 with a twins case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only רבי יהודה ever has split purity days, so the ברייתא must be his.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבנן can have split days, when a second twin interrupts the girl's purity days.

steps.title: Twins: the boy's impure days do not split the girl's count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא for the רבנן. In a twins case, one might think the boy's טומאה pauses the girl's sixty-six days so they get spread out. The word 'יום' teaches that the sixty must be continuous.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: you might think that if she had twins, a girl first and a boy later, the טומאה of the second birth breaks into the middle of her count. Then she would count sixty-six days in pieces. So the פסוק says 'day': just as a day is one continuous stretch, the sixty days must all be continuous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 25 by showing what the ברייתא is saying in the twins case. This way the ברייתא can fit the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the boy's seven טמאה days act as a pause, after which she goes back to finish the girl's sixty-six. The ברייתא rejects this and says the sixty run straight through. So the ברייתא does not prove anything about רבי יהודה, because the רבנן can also have a 'spread out' case to rule against.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it means: the גמרא is explaining the source's meaning
Twins
It interrupts, cuts in
Spread out, not in a row
Continuous, one right after another
The פסוק teaches, which shows we cannot think this

steps.whatToRemember: Even according to the רבנן there is a case where days could seem spread out: twins, a girl and then a boy. The ברייתא says no, the sixty stay continuous, so the ברייתא is no proof for רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'spreading' here does not come from a new birth restarting the count. It comes from the boy's seven טמאה days pausing the girl's purity days, which would then be picked up again afterward.

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the ברייתא about sixty continuous days, now being read the way the רבנן would read it.

phrases.english: One might think: where she gave birth to twins,
a girl first and a boy afterward,
the impurity of the birth should interrupt in the middle,
and she should count sixty-six days spread out?
So the verse says: 'day',
just as a day is entirely continuous,
so too the sixty are all continuous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 25 by explaining what the ברייתא teaches in the twins case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא as dealing with a specific case (twins) that fits the רבנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must follow רבי יהודה, since only he seems to have a case where days could be spread out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא can follow the רבנן: it rules out the idea that the boy's טומאה pauses the girl's sixty-six days.

steps.title: אביי's new source: the thirty days after a boy must be continuous
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings another ברייתא, this one about the thirty-three purity days after a boy. It says the thirty must be continuous and cannot be spread out.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear. The פסוק says 'thirty'. You might think the days count whether they are in a row or spread out. So the פסוק says 'day': just as a day is one continuous stretch, the thirty must be continuous too.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a new proof from a different ברייתא, this time about the purity days after a boy is born. The גמרא will now check whose opinion it fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twins answer worked for the sixty days of a girl, because a boy could be born during them. Here the ברייתא talks about the thirty days of a boy, so the twins idea (girl first, then boy) does not obviously apply. That makes this ברייתא a stronger test of who could be its author.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Thirty': part of the thirty-three purity days after a boy
One might have thought: introduces an idea the ברייתא will reject
Whether... or...: both options

phrases.english: Abaye said: Come and hear:
'Thirty':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:4, about a mother who gave birth to a boy: 'three days and thirty days'.

phrases.english: One might think, whether continuous or spread out?
So the verse says: 'day',
just as a day is entirely continuous,
so too the thirty are continuous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first ברייתא was shown to fit the רבנן, אביי brings a different ברייתא to try the question again.
steps.raayaObject: Who holds that a later birth could make purity days spread out, which seems to point to רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 12:4 saying the thirty days after a boy must be continuous

steps.title: Whose view is אביי's source? Could it be the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who wrote this ברייתא. It starts by suggesting the רבנן, then begins to ask whether the רבנן even hold of such a case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? If you say it is the רבנן, do the רבנן really hold...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it asks who wrote אביי's ברייתא and starts to argue it cannot be the רבנן. The rest of the question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as step 21. The גמרא is about to ask whether the רבנן have any case where a boy's thirty days could be spread out. If they don't, the ברייתא would have to follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
If you say: offers a possible answer that will be tested
But do they hold...? (a doubting question)

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
If you say the Rabbis,
but do the Rabbis hold...

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי הָא? אִלֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, וּמִי אִית לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts testing whose view אביי's ברייתא follows, like step 21 did for the first ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא wrote the ברייתא about the thirty continuous days, and whether the רבנן even have a case where those days could be spread out
